title: Assign a stable absolute @id to the site-level node
statement: The node describing the site as a whole carries an @id that is an absolute URL on the production origin and does not change between deployments, content edits, or template changes.
rationale: The identifier is what lets separate pages assert facts about the same site rather than about one site per page, so an identifier that changes breaks the connection retroactively for every page that used the old value.
implementation: Derive the identifier from the production origin plus a fixed fragment, declare it in one configuration constant, and reference that constant everywhere the site node is emitted or linked. Do not build it from a content identifier that editors can change.

verification.method: Collect the site-level node identifier from several routes and confirm every route reports the same absolute value.

title: Describe the publisher as a truthful Person or Organization
statement: The node named as publisher corresponds to the real legal or personal entity responsible for the content, and every property on it - name, url, logo, contact detail - is a fact about that entity.
rationale: The publisher node is the claim about who stands behind the content, so an invented organisation, a placeholder name, or a borrowed logo asserts something false about a real-world party.
implementation: Take the values from an existing authoritative record the site already publishes, such as an imprint, about page, or legal footer, and reference that single source from the generator. An automated agent must not supply a name, logo, address, or contact value that does not already appear somewhere the site publishes.

verification.method: Compare each publisher property against the corresponding value on the site's own imprint or about page and report properties with no such backing.

title: Connect each page node to the site node and its primary entity
statement: The page-level node references the site-level node through isPartOf and names the thing the page is principally about through mainEntity or mainEntityOfPage.
rationale: Without those references the page node is an isolated description that says the page exists but not what it belongs to or what it covers, which is the part a consumer assembling a picture of the site needs.
implementation: Emit both nodes in one graph per page and link them by identifier rather than by nesting a second copy of the site node inside the page node. Name the primary entity only where the page has one clear subject.

verification.method: Resolve the isPartOf and mainEntity references in the parsed graph and confirm each points at a node that the same graph or a declared identifier defines.

title: Keep the declared site name consistent with the visible brand name
statement: The name declared for the site in markup matches the name shown in the header, the title element suffix, and the site's own description of itself, allowing for a documented alternateName where a short form is genuinely in use.
rationale: Conflicting names across the same site give a consumer several candidate names for one entity, and the one it chooses is then outside the site's control.
implementation: Store the name once in configuration and read it from there in the markup generator, the layout header, and the title template. Add alternateName only for an abbreviation the site already displays, not for a keyword variant.

verification.method: Extract the declared name, the title element suffix, and the header brand text from the same response and report disagreement between them.

caution: Consistent naming is what the documentation asks a site to supply. Which name a search surface displays remains the surface's decision, so this control cannot promise a particular displayed name.

title: Use sameAs only for profiles the site can verify
statement: Each sameAs value points at an external profile that the entity described actually controls, and no value is added because the profile appears to match by name.
rationale: sameAs asserts that two identifiers denote the same thing, so a wrong value merges the site's entity with an unrelated party and the resulting confusion is not visible on the page that caused it.
implementation: Populate the list from profile links the site already publishes in its own footer or contact page, and treat any candidate not linked from the site as unverified. An automated agent must not search for and add external profiles on its own.

verification.method: Check every sameAs value against the outbound profile links the site itself publishes and report values with no such backing.

title: Detect entity references that resolve to no node in the graph
statement: Every identifier used as a reference in the emitted graph resolves either to a node defined in the same graph or to an identifier the site defines on another route it publishes.
rationale: A reference with nothing behind it looks structurally correct while carrying no information, and this is the usual result of deleting or renaming a node without updating the templates that pointed at it.
implementation: Collect the defined identifiers and the referenced identifiers across the routes the build produces, and fail the build on a reference with no definition. This is a consistency check over the site's own output and needs no external judgement.

verification.method: Build the sets of defined and referenced identifiers from the parsed graphs of all sampled routes and report the difference.
